Q: Rust memory ordering and atomics A:

"Happens-before" is something of a misnomer. A more accurate name would be "is-observable-before". IOW if f has side effects, then it is guaranteed that within the same thread g will see those side-effects, and any subsequent code will see both the effects of f and g. However this guarantee disappears between threads: it is possible for another thread to observe the effects of g without seeing the effects of f.

There are two causes why the guarantee disappears between threads:

  • As pointed out by @freakish in a comment, "happens-before" doesn't mean that the operations are physically realized in order: both the compiler and the CPU are allowed to reorder the operations so long as any code that depends on their effects still observes those effects in order.

  • On multi-core systems, it takes time for the effects of operations made by a specific core to become visible on the other cores. And barring memory barriers, there is no guarantee that all effects will travel at the same speed between cores. So even if the originating core ran the operations in order, the effects may become visible out of order in the other cores.

Q: Merge partition with C A:

Is the G: partition empty? You could (1) delete G:, (2) move the D: partition up leaving empty space between them, then (3) add the empty space to C:.

If G: is not empty, then you'll have to reduce the D: size before moving it.

Q: How do you find factors of a number and save the factors in an array for C? A:

Transcendental's answer is the right solution, but does not explain what has gone wrong with your code.

You are storing integers into characters. Setting aside issues where one of the factors may be too large to fit in a char, and assuming ASCII encoding, those integers represent characters that are not the ASCII representation of the character in question.

You also never null-terminate the array, but then you try to print it as a string. This leads to undefined behavior.
